title: Jyot Singh Becomes First Sikh and Indian American Elected to Georgia Legislature
excerpt: The 27-year-old Democrat won House District 97 in Gwinnett County with about 68% of the vote, defeating Republican Yassin Moghazy in the November 3 midterms.
body:
• Jyot Singh, 27, won Georgia House District 97 on November 3 with 13,820 votes (about 68%) to Republican Yassin Moghazy's 6,509 (about 32%), according to India Weekly.
  • He is the first Sikh American and the first Indian American elected to the Georgia General Assembly; results remain unofficial until the state certifies them.
  • District 97 covers parts of Duluth, Peachtree Corners and Norcross, plus all of Berkeley Lake, in Gwinnett County.
  • Singh, a Yale graduate and son of Sikh immigrants, takes office on January 11, 2027, as a member-elect.

Jyot Singh has made Georgia political history. The 27-year-old Democrat won the state's House District 97 seat in the November 3 midterm elections, becoming the first Sikh American and the first Indian American elected to the Georgia General Assembly, according to India Weekly and multiple community outlets.

India Weekly reported Singh secured 13,820 votes, or 68 per cent of the total, against Republican Yassin Moghazy's 6,509 votes, or 32 per cent. Election-night trackers had shown a similar margin while counting continued. The results are unofficial until the state certifies them, the Education Times noted. Singh announced the win on X, thanking Georgia.

An open seat in Gwinnett County

District 97 sits in Gwinnett County, one of the most diverse counties in the American South, covering parts of Duluth, Peachtree Corners and Norcross, along with all of Berkeley Lake. It was an open seat: the incumbent, state Representative Ruwa Romman, ran instead for Georgia Senate District 7.

Singh built his path through the May 19 Democratic primary, where he beat Jacques Laurent with about 59 per cent of the vote to Laurent's 40 per cent, carrying every precinct in the district, according to community reporting.

From a working-class household to Yale — and back

Singh is the son of Sikh immigrants from India and grew up in a working-class family in Norcross. He attended Yale University on a full scholarship and graduated in 2021, and works as a civil rights advocate and small business owner in Gwinnett County. His biography — an immigrant household, a scholarship to an Ivy League university, and a return to organise in the community he grew up in — was central to how his campaign presented itself.

Part of a wider wave

Singh's win was one of at least 30 Indian American victories in state legislative races in the 2026 midterms, out of 41 candidates tracked in post-election tallies — a wave that also included Pooja Sethi's landmark win in Texas House District 47. But Georgia's is the breakthrough with no precedent: in the state's history, no Sikh American and no Indian American had previously been elected to its legislature. Singh is listed as a member-elect, with his term set to begin on January 11, 2027.

For Georgia's Indian American community — concentrated in the same Gwinnett suburbs Singh will represent — the seat converts demographic presence into direct representation at the state capitol for the first time.
